metadata.title: zhangdx2025/tree-mortality-soil-carbon: v1.0.0 — Analysis code for Topographic Decoupling of Tree-Mortality Disturbances Drives Contrasting Soil Carbon Fates via Divergent Microbial Strategies
metadata.description:
Overview

This release archives the R code used to process data, perform statistical analyses, train machine-learning models, generate figures, and save numerical outputs for the revised manuscript:

Topographic Decoupling of Tree-Mortality Disturbances Drives Contrasting Soil Carbon Fates via Divergent Microbial Strategies

Contents

This release includes:

  • Eleven numbered analysis scripts covering data processing, statistical analyses, genome-informed microbial trait analyses, XGBoost model training, SHAP analyses, metagenomic gene-abundance analyses, figure generation, and numerical output generation.
  • Scripts associated with Figs. 1–5, Supplementary Figs. 1–8, and Supplementary Tables 1–5.
  • A subset of small supporting data files required by the scripts.
  • Documentation of the analysis workflow, software environment, approximate runtimes, and required folder structure.

Associated data

The complete processed dataset and saved analysis outputs are available in Zenodo (V2):

https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20849331

Raw sequence data are available in the China National GeneBank Sequence Archive under the following project accessions:

  • Amplicon sequencing data: CNP0008410
  • Shotgun metagenomic sequencing data: CNP0008455

Reproducibility

The analyses were conducted in R v4.5.1. The required R packages are loaded within the individual scripts.

For a complete rerun, users should download the processed data and saved analysis outputs from Zenodo, arrange them according to the folder structure described in the README, and run scripts 01–11 in numerical order. Saved analysis outputs may also be used to reproduce figures and tables without rerunning the most computationally intensive steps.

metadata.description:
Demonstration release – Machine learning models and scripts

This release contains the custom scripts and supporting resources specifically related to the machine learning models developed for the study.

The complete data science workflow, including the Galaxy-based analysis pipeline, workflow definitions, and the associated scripts required for the full computational analysis, is distributed through the Galaxy platform provided as a Docker container, as described in the associated manuscript:

https://hub.docker.com/r/dockervito/galaxybiounicam4

This repository is therefore intended as a complementary resource for accessing and reproducing the machine learning components of the analysis. It does not contain the complete Galaxy workflow environment, which is provided through the Dockerized Galaxy platform.

This release is archived to provide a stable and citable version of the machine learning resources associated with the study and to support transparency and reproducibility of the reported analyses.

metadata.title: genenull: gene-identity null models for ClinVar benchmarks
metadata.description:
A model scored only by the pathogenic fraction of a variant's own gene — no sequence, no structure, no conservation — reaches AUROC 0.921 on 197,904 ClinVar missense variants under a random 10-fold split, against 0.955–0.963 for four current predictors. Under within-gene evaluation the predictor ranking inverts, and across 22 dbNSFP predictors roughly half the advantage conventional benchmarks give clinically supervised models is gene identity rather than variant-level discrimination.

Contains the genenull module, the analysis pipeline, the figure scripts, the pre-registered predictor exposure classification, and every result table the manuscript reports.

metadata.title: IAUC Systematic Literature Review: Extraction Protocol, Metadata, and Validation Data
metadata.description:
Data and code archive for a systematic review of the urban climate literature, in which large language models extracted structured metadata from the full text of every paper in the corpus.

Contents

  • data/extracted_metadata/ — 9,284 canonical per-paper JSON records
  • data/enrichments/ and data/contribution_rationales/ — 9,284 per-paper enrichment and rationale records
  • data/volunteer_review/ — anonymised expert validation responses
  • data/cross_model_validation/ — model comparisons supporting the extraction choice, plus later isolated noncanonical GPT-5.6 audits that do not replace the canonical corpus or feed manuscript results
  • src/, tests/, Makefile, and uv.lock — the analysis pipeline and paper-reproducibility test suite

Reproducing the analysis

uv sync --extra dev then make paper-all rebuilds the consolidated corpus and manuscript statistics. make ci-test runs the offline tests shipped with the package.

Licensing

Everything in this deposit — data and code alike — is released under CC-BY-4.0.

This version

Refreshes the revised-manuscript archive after the final plotting audit and adds portable records from subsequent, explicitly noncanonical extraction comparisons. Canonical Gemini records, corpus membership, and manuscript results are unchanged.

Axiomatic Constraint Compilation and Discrete Mechanics

A Linear Synthesis of Scalar Algebras, Action Emergence, and State-Space Addressability

Driven by Dean Kulik

July 2026

 

 

Scientific models have historically operated on substance-based ontologies, treating matter, space, and time as foundational entities governed by external physical laws. An alternative paradigm—the constraint-compilation framework—reconstructs physical and computational reality from an axiomatic foundation based on the operational limits of state transitions. By establishing a small set of primitive constraints governing system updates, higher-order physical structures—including local conservation laws, the complex scalar field, Hamilton's principle, gauge symmetries, and discrete permutation mechanics—are derived directly as mathematical necessities.

The core mechanism across all these domains is addressability in change: a constrained system expands its effective capability not by violating its underlying rules, but by discovering new representation spaces and orthogonal channels that exploit latent structural addressability. This report provides a linear synthesis of the complete theoretical framework and empirical corpus. It details the axiomatic pipeline, extracts all compiled theorems and novel quantitative measurements, and outlines the structural audit trail governing the framework's internal consistency.

Primitive Constraint Architecture and Topological State Space

The framework begins with five irreducible primitive constraints that define the admissibility of state space configurations. These constraints do not act as external rules applied to pre-existing objects; rather, they define the topological boundaries outside of which no physical or computational state can exist.

Constraint 0 establishes that distinction exists (). It defines the undifferentiated ground state, where total global connection behaves locally as a void. Graph-theoretically, Constraint 0 is represented by a complete graph  whose Laplacian matrix  yields a spectrum of vibrational modes consisting of a single zero eigenvalue with multiplicity 1 (representing global monolithic translation) and an excited eigenvalue  with multiplicity  (representing maximal connectivity and stiffness). Traversing a boundary walk on a 12-cell cylindrical manifold yields a stasis period of 12 steps across a single face, whereas introducing an offset seam transforms the topology into a Möbius strip with a face-parity twist, forcing a 24-step traversal that serializes superposition into temporal sequence.

Constraint 1 mandates continuation: every admissible state  must admit at least one legal successor  () under the transition algebra. Terminal states and static fixed points are strictly excluded. Topologically, Constraint 1 mandates a nowhere-vanishing vector field on the compact state manifold . By the Poincaré-Hopf theorem, the sum of the indices of the vector field's zeros equals the Euler characteristic ; because zeros are forbidden, the manifold must satisfy .

Constraint 1a establishes independence preservation: independent distinctions remain independently continuable. For independent continuation operators  and , joint evolution must factor as , enforcing the algebraic commutation condition . This single commutator serves as a structural spine operating across three distinct layers: at the transition algebra layer it eliminates coordination channels to enforce local conservation; at the scalar algebra layer it forces commutativity to select the complex numbers; and at the symmetry layer it constrains gauge sector factorization.

Constraint 2 enforces history preservation: every continuation preserves the set of states reachable from prior history, forbidding the deletion of accessible nodes from the transition graph. Iterated transition functions over finite sets yield descending chains  which inevitably terminate at a fixed point . To prevent the flow of possibility from freezing, Constraint 2 forces the physical state space to possess infinite degrees of freedom.

Constraint 5 defines the observable event primitive: an observable event is the minimal continuation simultaneously carrying two independent degrees of freedom, continuous spatial propagation and a distinct temporal residue. Constraint 5 forces the real dimension of the scalar continuation algebra to satisfy , while spontaneous symmetry breaking eliminates the static vacuum as a forbidden fixed point.

Rigorously auditing the primitive set demonstrates that initial formulations contained redundant axioms. At the binary base (), Constraint 1 alone forces the unique legal state transition map to be bijective (the swap map), rendering Constraint 2 derivable rather than primitive at the foundational layer. Similarly, uniform in-degree and isotropic change are derived directly from Constraint 1 when combined with a discrete difference operator.

The Division Algebra Theorem and Complex Continuation Amplitudes

Standard quantum field theory postulates complex-valued probability amplitudes. The Division Algebra Theorem replaces axiomatic postulation with a proof demonstrating that the complex field  is the unique admissible scalar continuation algebra under the primitive constraint set .

The mathematical derivation reduces the candidate algebras through a four-stage elimination process:

First, the scalar weight algebra  over the state space must be a finite-dimensional division algebra over . Constraints 0 and 1 forbid zero divisors, as  for  terminates a lawful state. By Frobenius' Theorem (1877), the only associative finite-dimensional division algebras over  are the real numbers  (dimension 1), the complex numbers  (dimension 2), and the quaternions  (dimension 4).

Second, algebras containing zero divisors—such as the direct product algebra —are physically inadmissible. In , element-wise multiplication yields . Two non-zero, lawful continuation amplitudes compose to generate an absolute zero state, creating a Constraint 1-forbidden terminal fixed point.

Third, the real numbers  are eliminated because  carries a single real degree of freedom. Its only intrinsic linear transformation generates , a disconnected discrete group. Constraint 5 requires continuous spatial phase rotations via , which cannot be realized over  without introducing a second real dimension, thereby forcing the transition from  to .

Fourth, the quaternions  are eliminated via algebraic simplicity.  is non-commutative () and simple as a real algebra, possessing only trivial two-sided ideals ( and ). For any algebra homomorphism , the kernel  must be either  (faithful) or  (trivial). If faithful,  is injective and inherits 's non-commutativity, yielding . Applying independent phase updates to independent subsystems produces ordering-dependent outcomes, directly violating Constraint 1a. If trivial,  maps all elements to zero, exiting  entirely. No intermediate representation exists.

The complex field  uniquely survives all compiled constraints, possessing continuous phase rotation , commutativity under Constraint 1a, and exact two-dimensional minimality under Methodological Principle .  emerges directly as the automorphism group of the compiled scalar field.

Classical and quantum mechanics postulate Hamilton's principle (). Within this framework, action is compiled directly as the accumulated transition cost of discrete paths under Constraints 0 through 5.

Synthesis

The compilation chain established across these theoretical and empirical results demonstrates that physical laws represent the compiled requirements of continuation under immutable constraints. State space initialization begins with Constraint 0 ground state cancellations combined with Constraint 1 continuation mandates, forcing admissible state space manifolds to satisfy . Algebraic selection via Constraints 0, 1, 1a, 2, and 5 systematically eliminates non-field, one-dimensional, and non-commutative algebras, isolating the complex numbers  as the unique scalar field for physical amplitudes.

Transition costs on spatial adjacency graphs converge to the free-field Lagrangian, where local Constraint 1-consistency requires a vanishing transition residual (), establishing Hamilton's principle () as a compiled theorem. By tracking state space transitions through explicit algebraic operations, the constraint-compilation framework provides a unified, fully deterministic model of physical and computational mechanics.

metadata.title: New insights into estimating the cementation exponent of the tight and deep carbonate pore systems via rigorous numerical strategies
metadata.description: One of the main constituents of any reservoir characterization is an accurate forecast of water saturation, which is highly dependent upon the cementation exponent. Even though there have been a lot of studies, the most common correlations depend on total porosity. This means that they do not work as well in heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs, especially tight formations with total porosities less than 10%. This study aims to develop accurate and universal models for estimating the cementation exponent in deep and tight carbonate pore systems located in West Asia. Two heuristic algorithms, including the radial basis function neural network optimized by ant colony optimization (RBFNN-ACO) and gene expression programming (GEP), were employed to calculate the cementation exponent. To do this, we prepared a databank incorporating cementation exponents, total porosity, and various pore types. Then, the databank is classified into the test subset (for model prediction checking) and the train subset (for model construction). The reliability of the new recommended models is inspected by applying several statistical quality measures associated with graphical analyses. So, the consequences of the modeling disclose the large precision of the above-mentioned RBFNN-ACO, GEP Model-I, and GEP Model-II by average absolute percentage relative deviations (AAPRD%) of 6.28%, 6.39%, and 7.45%, respectively. Based on the outliers analysis, nearly 95% of the databank and model estimations are, respectively, valid and reliable. Additionally, the three input variables, including moldic porosity (with a + 70% impact value), non-fabric-selective dissolution (connected) porosity (with a -30% impact value), and interparticle porosity (with a -23% impact value), exhibit the main affecting parameters on the cementation exponent. Comparing current results with traditional literature correlations demonstrates the supremacy of the RBFNN-ACO model (AAPRD = 6.28% and root mean squared error (RMSE) = 0.17) over the examined literature correlations such as Borai’s equation (AAPRD = 12.30% and RMSE = 0.41). In addition, RBFNN-ACO can give better results than Borai’s Eqn. for tight (porosity less than 10%) and deep carbonate samples.

metadata.title: Cutting Tool Wear Minimization in Machining Operations: A Review
metadata.description: Cutting tool wear significantly influences machining performance, surface quality, and manufacturing cost. Proper minimization of cutting tool wear will result in enhanced life of the cutting tool, surface integrity, precision, and sustainability of the machining process. There are various methods for minimizing cutting tool wear in machining operations. These include the optimization of parameters such as reducing the feed and speed, use of proper coating such as TiN and Al2O3, lubrication/cooling, and proper material for the cutting tool like carbide and ceramic materials. The application of chip breakers and high machine rigidity can minimize wear by lowering heat and friction, which are the major causes of wear. Reduction in wear will ensure a better surface finish, enhanced tool life, and economic efficiency of the machining process. The main objective of this research paper is to conduct an extensive study on wear of cutting tools in machining operations. As a result, the study discusses several advanced methods of tool wear detection in cutting tools, including sensor-based methods, machine vision, and AI/ML-assisted predictive maintenance. Additionally, a critical assessment in tool wear minimization is conducted to apply new material to the cutting tool, the coating process, cutting parameter and path optimization, cooling and lubrication systems such as minimum amount lubrication and cryogenic cooling. Moreover, various challenges with intelligent and autonomous manufacturing systems that arise in tool wear prediction with regard to availability of data and reliability of prediction models are discussed in the study. Finally, potential future research directions are provided, with an emphasis on the importance of using digital twin technologies and sustainable manufacturing approaches in tool wear management.

metadata.title: More Completeness Results for Abstraction Logic
metadata.description:
We start with an arbitrary well-formed abstraction logic, retaining its full
binding signature and all of its original axioms, including axioms with
binding premises, and study three enrichments. For material implication we
add implication introduction, material modus ponens, Peirce's law, and
classical lift. If the original signature is countable and the variable
supply is countably infinite, the resulting calculus is sound and
formula-complete with respect to material classical general models of the
original logic. A ranked Henkin-style construction proves this for every
formula in the full language, without any further restriction on the original
axioms. For identity equality we add reflexivity, Leibniz, and a higher-order
congruence rule for every abstraction. The resulting calculus is sound and
formula-complete with respect to classical general models in which equality
expresses identity of carrier values, for arbitrary signatures and original
axioms and with no countability assumption. Under the countability
assumptions of the material case, the combined calculus is sound and
formula-complete with respect to classical general models satisfying both
semantic conditions. The corresponding completeness problem for Heyting
general models already contains Kuznetsov's open problem of whether every
intermediate propositional logic is complete with respect to complete Heyting
algebras.

data.title: More Completeness Results for Abstraction Logic

metadata.title: Association between Personality Traits, Work-Family Conflict, Job Stress and Nurses' Cognitive Failures: A Cross-Sectional Study
metadata.description: Background: Cognitive failures are one of the most important causes of patients' unsafe events. Hence, it is necessary to consider individual and cognitive, as well as extra-organizational characteristics. The present study was conducted to investigate the association between personality traits, job stress, work-family conflict and nurses' cognitive failures. Materials and Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 250 nurses working in three public hospitals in Sari city, Iran, in 2021. The subjects were selected using Stratified Random Sampling. NEO Five-Factor Inventory, Health and Safety Executive (HSE) tool, Work-Family Conflict Scale (WFCS), and Occupational Cognitive Failure Questionnaire (OCFQ) were used to measure personality traits, job stress, work-family conflict, and cognitive Failures, respectively. The data were analyzed in SPSS (ve. 23) and regression analysis with the sequential method was applied. Results: Among 13 studied predictor variables, only extraversion, agreeableness, demand, and role were predictors of cognitive failures. These variables explain 44.1% of the variance of cognitive failure. The Β values of neuroticism and conscientiousness to predict cognitive failures were 0.34 and -0.29, respectively (P < 0.001). Although role (Β = 0.15, p < 0.001) and demand (Β = 0.14, p < 0.001) significantly predict cognitive failure; however, their effect is limited. The results of the study did not provide confirmation for the moderating effect of neuroticism, extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness on the association between work-family conflict, job stress, and cognitive failures. Conclusions: Along with environmental and organizational stress factors, evaluating nurses’ personality traits is necessary to control cognitive failures.
